newsitem.title: UK: Dlr extends gains in Europe after overnight lows.
newsitem.headline: Dlr extends gains in Europe after overnight lows.

text.p: The dollar crept higher in morning Europe, extending a mild recovery from its overnight lows seen after steady U.S. rates post-FOMC and the ongoing prospect of higher Japan rates.
The decision by the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meeting Tuesday to leave U.S. rates on hold took out some dollar support but mainly against the mark.

Dollar/yen suffered overnight after a senior Bank of Japan official was quoted as saying the central bank was considering the timing of a rate hike decision. Later, a BOJ spokesman said policy was still geared to economic recovery.

"What the government is indicating is the recovery would gather strength," said Gerard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International in London. "But the authorities don't want the yen to appreciate too far, and comments will be geared to stabilising the foreign exchange rates."
Dollar/yen was trading at 113.90/4.00 at 0755 GMT, up from overnight lows below 113 and late Tuesday's level of 113.65/75.

"The FOMC decision and BOJ comments haven't had a lasting impact. We're seeing signs of fresh investor buying this morning," said a U.S. bank dealer. "We expect a few days of consolidation but people seem to be bargain-hunting here."

The Federal Reserve's decision not to hike U.S. rates was given a cautious response by U.S. bonds, suggesting expectations are still high for tightening later this year. Dealers said these expectations were also serving to limit dollar weakness.
Dollar/mark was trading at 1.6908/13 at 0815 GMT after touching an earlier peak of 1.6920 marks and well above overnight lows just above 1.67. It stood at 1.6960/70 Tuesday.
Market focus was on U.S. March trade data due at 1230 GMT today. An average of analysts' forecasts point to a $10.3 billion deficit, little changed from February's $10.4 billion shortfall.
German April M3 money supply data is due from this week with growth expected to shrink to 7.7 percent against fourth quarter 1996 from 8.3 percent in March.
But analysts said the German data, and Germany's Ifo research institute survey for April due Thursday, are unlikely to change the weak outlook for the German mark.
"The German economy is much weaker than the market says," said DKB's Lyons. "The prospect of a soft euro and the weakness of the domestic economy will keep the mark relatively soft."
The Swiss franc eased from its recent gains against the mark and dollar in morning trade.

The Swiss franc retreated after the Swiss National Bank said it will continue to add liquidity significantly to counter recent franc strength. The central bank said the franc's recent gains had no fundamental basis.
Dealers said recent speculation of a Swiss rate hike and the franc's 'safe haven' status in the recent dollar volatility and Europe's monetary union jitters were said to be factors.
"But we see these as belated explanations for what has really been a technical move," said the U.S. bank dealer.
